summary: The comment opposes extending CIPA to third-party-owned devices, arguing that this would undermine privacy protections. The FCC is urged to conduct an independent, industry-neutral scientific assessment of RF exposure risks and implement transparent, evidence-based policies to protect public health. The comment calls for the FCC to consider ecological and health impacts of RF radiation before proceeding with rulemaking on cell towers and wireless infrastructure. It cites external evidence that new cell tower transmitters would increase involuntary exposure to RF radiation, which poses public health risks to humans and wildlife. The International Commission on the Biological Effects of Electromagnetic Fields (ICBE-EMF) discusses the precautionary principle in environmental science, emphasizing its role in informing policy and protecting human health and the environment. The comment text is not directly related to FCC E-Rate but provides context on the principle's application in environmental policy. The text argues against the sunset of E-Rate programs, citing legal authority and precedent.
filer_raw: Theodora Scarato | Director of Wireless and EMF Program at Environmental Health Sciences
